title: Personnel changes in Bunk's band: drummers and pianists
summary: Blumberg recalls Baby Dodds's playing and dissension, and the three drummers and two pianists across both engagements.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Did you see many of the changes in the personnel that you, uh, around observed when one guy came in and watch the difference in the band?
Uh, the only guy I didn't get a chance to hear too much, as I recall, was Kaiser Marshall. I don't think I heard him. Uh-huh. I heard, I might have heard him one time.
Well, who was the first guy to leave the band, out of the original?
I guess it was Baby. I mean, I, I'm really vague on these things. Uh-huh. I'd say all I have is a, a bunch of impressions for the most part.
Fragmentary, fragmentary. Oh, yeah, well, uh, definitely when Baby was playing well, I think that nobody could approach him. Uh, but there just got to be, uh, so much dissension there that, uh.
Well, Baby had his problems and Bunk had his problems.

Uh. Uh. Yeah, so they, the only changes in personnel were, as far as I can recall, uh, uh, there were three drummers and two piano players. There was Baby, Kaiser Marshall, and, and, uh, Al Steele. This is, uh, the two engagements. Oh. And, uh, there was, uh, Alton Purnell and, and Don Ewell. Uh, there might have been maybe a third piano player sometime that I didn't know about, but as, as I recall, those, those are the ones.
